name: Provenance of Research Images and Data
title: Provenance of Research Images and Data
answer: Provenance of research images and data concerns the documented origin, processing history, and chain of custody for visual and tabular evidence used in scientific work. It covers raw acquisition, any transformations, and the metadata that ties a result back to its source. In AI research, this includes training datasets, generated figures, and reused benchmark data. The goal is to make every image and dataset traceable to its original instrument, repository, or author.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Provenance of research images and data concerns the documented origin, processing history, and chain of custody for visual and tabular evidence used in scientific work. It covers raw acquisition, any transformations, and the metadata that ties a result back to its source. In AI research, this includes training datasets, generated figures, and reused benchmark data. The goal is to make every image and dataset traceable to its original instrument, repository, or author.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Provenance systems rely on persistent identifiers, versioned data repositories, and cryptographic hashing to record changes. Research institutions and publishers use electronic lab notebooks, data management plans, and image repositories that store original files alongside derived versions. For AI work, model cards and dataset cards often carry provenance fields, and the site's catalogue of 732 tools includes utilities for checksum verification and metadata extraction. Content on this site links to the original paper rather than to a search tool, so the underlying source remains the reference point.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A researcher records the instrument, settings, date, and operator at capture, then logs every processing step such as cropping, contrast adjustment, or normalization. For datasets, each record includes its source, license, and any filtering or augmentation applied. Reviewers and integrity officers compare submitted images against raw files and metadata, and automated tools flag duplicated regions or inconsistent timestamps. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,555 extracted claims supports this by keeping the original publication attached to each assertion.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance records carry rights information such as licenses, consent for human-derived data, and conditions for reuse. Risks include image manipulation, data leakage between training and test sets, and unattributed reuse of third-party material. Institutions address these through data stewardship policies, preregistration, and audit trails that show who accessed or altered a file. The site's 91 AI books and 674 glossary terms provide background on the norms, but the actual governance sits with funders, journals, and research organizations.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Provenance is moving toward machine-readable chains of custody that can be checked automatically during submission and review. Persistent identifiers and decentralized ledgers are being tested for recording dataset versions and image edits without a central authority. As generative models make synthetic images easier to produce, provenance standards will likely require cryptographic signing at the point of creation. The site's 801 scientific models may eventually include provenance metadata as a standard field, making origin checks part of normal model evaluation.
